name_reason: Compliant with global naming convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. domain=animation; descriptor=summon_variant_e_16slot_sprite_base_table reflects both purpose (per-slot sprite-id base table for the variant-E 16-slot summon-spell animation) and data type (_table = const array). No Ghidra address residue in the name: 'variant_e' is the summon-animation variant family selector and '16slot' is the slot count (16, matching the uint8[16] dimension), both domain semantics, not the data address 0x52539. Confirmed datatype byte[16] (Ghidra LEN=16) matches the [16] dimension in the name.
purpose: Per-slot sprite-id base table for the variant-E 16-slot summon-spell animation; each entry is the base sprite id added to that slot's frame counter to select the blit sprite.
logic_summary: 16-entry const uint8 table. Sole reader fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_e_16slot (@ 0x274B0, entry #8 of the 10-entry summon-tick dispatch table) REP-MOVSD-copies all 16 bytes (ECX=4 -> 4 dwords = 16 bytes; src ESI=0x52539 at 0x274D1) into a local stack buffer abStack_20 in the prologue. During TICK states (state_code 2/5) each slot loads its base via MOVZX byte ptr [ESP+EBX*1+0xC] (0x27557) and computes sprite_id = frame_counter[slot] + table[slot], passed to fd2_blit_indexed_sprite. The bytes form an 8-entry pattern {0,8,24,16,8,0,24,16} repeated twice, producing a 4-quadrant cycling layout in sprite-strip space as the staggered frame counters advance.
element_semantics: uint8 per-slot sprite-id base offset (one byte per animation slot, 16 slots). Value range observed 0..24. Added to the slot's signed frame counter (data_fd2_battle_summon_anim_variant_e_16slot_frame_counter_array[slot]) to form the sprite id for fd2_blit_indexed_sprite. The first 8 entries {0,8,24,16,8,0,24,16} are repeated for slots 8..15.
notes: is_const=true: zero write-xrefs in game code; only a READ xref (0x274D1 MOVSD source) plus its base-address DATA xref (0x274CC); src already declares const uint8[...] and segment is .object2 .rodata. src comment block (anitab.c lines 413-434) is already precise, accurate, ASCII, and fully consistent with disassembly (REP-MOVSD ECX=4 -> 16 bytes; MOVZX EBX*1 stride proving uint8; sprite_id = frame_counter+base; no writers) and with the live bytes 00 08 18 10 08 00 18 10 00 08 18 10 08 00 18 10 -> comment_verdict=keep, no Edit made.
